checks.claim: C1: Interval-area F formula, symmetry, and normalization of all 15 white order-four diagrams (9 distinct rows plus chain exchange), with paired time gaps and chain horizons
checks.reason: Take a>=b. The corner {x-y>=c} of [-a,a]x[-b,b] is empty for c>=a+b. For a-b<=c<=a+b it is a right triangle with legs a+b-c. For c<a-b it is a trapezoid of area 2b(a-c). So the area is 4ab, 4ab-(a+b-c)^2 and 4bc respectively, and (E:interval-area) reproduces all three, since (a+b-c)^2-(a-b-c)^2=4b(a-c). Symmetry: swapping x and y gives F(b,a,c), and the unimodular map (x,y)->(x,x-y) gives F(a,c,b). With chains rooted at 0 and increment variables, I re-derived every position list, Green constraint, area and pair gap independently. (0,4): A area 4ac, gaps b,d; B area 4a min(b,c,d), gaps b+c, c+d; C area 4a min(b,d), gaps b+c+d, c. (1,3) with single time r: A area 4 min(r,a) b, gaps |r-a|, c; B area F(r,a,min(b,c)), gaps |r-a-b|, b+c; C area F(r,a,c), gaps |r-a-b-c|, b. (2,2): A area 4ac, gaps b,d; B area 4min(a,c)min(b,d), gaps |a-c|, |a+b-c-d|; C area F(a,c,min(b,d)), gaps |a-c-d|, |a+b-c|. Each wave factor contributes 1/2, giving 1/16, and each unit-mass delta removes one coordinate, so V = area/16 matches every row. The chain horizons (sum of increments < t in each chain, and 0<r<t) are correct. Chain exchange relabels the four vertices bijectively on Pi_2: for (3,1) it maps A->C, B->B, C->A relative to (1,3), and (4,0) maps identically. All 15 terms are therefore covered, and the multiplicities 2,2,1 in (E:total-four) are right. Scaling gives t^4 (measure) x t^2 (area) x t^{-2 alpha0} = t^{6-2 alpha0}.

checks.claim: C2: Distributional white-noise reduction, boundary sets, uniform spatial bound and temporal integrability
checks.reason: With mass-one smoothed deltas, change variables to (x, u=y_j-y_i, y, w=y_l-y_k). The regularized spatial factor is then the integral of p(u)p(w)Psi(u,w), where Psi is 1/16 times the area of a polygon cut out by interval indicators. For positive increments those indicators converge pointwise off their boundaries, which have two-dimensional measure zero. So Psi is continuous at (0,0), and the approximate identity gives Psi(0,0), which is the displayed area. Uniform bound: the Green factors confine all positions to [-1,1] at unit time. Each smoothed delta then integrates to at most 2 over its paired coordinates, giving 2^2/16 = 1/4 uniformly in the smoothing. The temporal weights are dominated on the unit cube by a product over two disjoint label pairs, which is integrable for alpha0<1. Temporal truncation in the source satisfies gamma^0_delta <= |.|^{-alpha0}. Dominated convergence therefore passes the regularized integrals to the table without pointwise delta evaluation. The written argument is terse (see minor findings) but complete in substance.

checks.claim: C3: Fixed-order alpha0 -> 0 dominated convergence using disjoint labels and enlarged cubes
checks.reason: On the unit domain all original times lie in [0,1], so |s-r| <= 1 and |s-r|^{-alpha0} <= |s-r|^{-abar} for 0 <= alpha0 <= abar < 1. The increment-to-time map is unimodular within each chain, so the domain can be enlarged to [0,1]^4. The two pairs use disjoint labels, so the dominator factorizes as (2/((1-abar)(2-abar)))^2; I confirmed that this value is the integral of |s-r|^{-abar} over [0,1]^2. The spatial factor (<= 1/4) does not depend on alpha0. Dominated convergence gives the limit as the alpha0=0 integral in every row. For Riesz, the same Tonelli bound with fixed abar applies, because the spatial Riesz factors do not depend on alpha0.

checks.claim: C4: Exact static sector integrals, all nine table entries, reflection factor, factorial denominators, and the total 11/540
checks.reason: Integrating the time slacks first gives the simplex volume (1-L)_+^n/n!. Together with the 1/16, this proves (E:static-sector). The length pairs match the position lists. The three sectors and their point reflections tile the plane and preserve |x|, |y| and w, which gives the factor 2. Each substitution is unimodular. I recomputed all 27 sector integrals by hand. Here I(p,q;N) = 1/(pq(N+1)(N+2)) handles the single-constraint cases. Beta integrals handle (1,3)A/B S2 (3/160), (1,3)A S3 (11/480), (1,3)B S3 (11/1440) and (2,2)C S1/S2 (31/1440). The substitution a=2u+v, b=u+2v with Jacobian 1/3 gives (2,2)C S3: (1/3)(1/9 - 98/1440) = 31/2160. Row factors are 1/192, 1/48 and 1/32. These give 1/2880, 1/8640, 1/5760; 1/576, 29/34560, 1/640; 1/144, 1/480, 31/17280. Row sums are 11/17280, 143/34560 and 187/17280. Also 2(11/17280) + 2(143/34560) + 187/17280 = 352/17280 = 11/540. As a third independent check, I integrated the table V entries directly over Dirichlet simplices using min(.,.) = integral of a product of indicators. This reproduces 1/2880, 1/5760, 1/8640, 1/576, 1/144 and 1/480. The order-two value 2c0 at alpha0=0 is 2/6 = 1/3. static-controls.json agrees with every value, and the Sobol and root Monte Carlo diagnostics are consistent.

checks.claim: C5: Riesz order-two formulas, constants, powers, admissible parameters, static limit and normalized white limit
checks.reason: Phi(x) = |x|^{2-alpha}/((1-alpha)(2-alpha)) has Phi'' = |x|^{-alpha}. This gives the integral of |y-z|^{-alpha} over [-s,s]x[-r,r] as 2(Phi(s+r)-Phi(s-r)). Multiplying by 1/4 and c_alpha yields the displayed kernel. Doubling over s>r, setting v=s-r and integrating r over (0,t-v) gives exactly the E X_1^2 formula. For E X_2, the spatial factor is c_alpha r v^{1-alpha}/(1-alpha), and the Beta integral of r v^{1-alpha-alpha0} over r+v<t gives t^beta/((2-alpha-alpha0)(3-alpha-alpha0)(4-alpha-alpha0)). Admissibility holds: alpha<1 (local integrability in d=1), alpha0<1, and alpha+alpha0<2 is automatic. Static check: the integral of (s+r)^{2-alpha}-|s-r|^{2-alpha} over [0,1]^2 is (2^{4-alpha}-4)/((3-alpha)(4-alpha)), and adding 2E X_2 gives c_alpha 2^{3-alpha}/((1-alpha)(2-alpha)(3-alpha)(4-alpha)). With c_alpha=(1-alpha)/2 this tends to 1/3. At fixed alpha0 the normalized E X_2 tends to c0/2. For E X_1^2 the bracket tends to (1-v)^2 and the prefactor to 1/2, giving (1/2)B(1-alpha0,3) = c0, with dominator C v^{-alpha0}. The formula value is consistent with the floating check in numerical-controls.json (about 1.714 at alpha=alpha0=1/2, matching my rough Simpson estimate of 1.717).

checks.claim: C6: Riesz order-four representation: independent uniforms, product of h_l, domains, all pairings, homogeneity and finiteness
checks.reason: (1/2)1_{[-h,h]} equals h times the law of hU with U uniform on [-1,1], so each Green factor contributes h_l and the 1/16 is absorbed correctly. Green factors factor over increments, so the U_l are independent across both chains. Positions Y_l and times S_l restart at each chain's first index b(l), and the map is unimodular. H_m with an empty sum equal to 0 covers all five splits, and D ranges over A, B, C on the global labels. Scaling h -> t h gives t^4 (measure) x t^4 (product of h) x t^{-2 alpha0} x t^{-2 alpha} = t^{2 beta}. Finiteness: enlarge to [0,1]^4 x [-1,1]^4 and bound the indicators by one. The time and space singular factors each involve two disjoint pairs and are integrable for alpha0, alpha < 1, so Tonelli applies. The bound is uniform for alpha0 <= abar, which also justifies the static Riesz M_4 limit. The representation is correctly described as not closed-form.

checks.claim: C7: Source calibration, no disputed Chen-Hu constant, no exchange of limits, coefficient versus asymptotic-constant distinction, polynomial-truncation limitation
checks.reason: The image confirms Chen-Hu Theorem 1.2, (1.9), p.2147. Its exponent is (4-alpha)/(3-alpha) under (1.8) with 0<alpha<2^d or alpha=d=1, which covers both G1 cases. As alpha0 -> 0, both kappa and rho tend to this exponent. Corollary 1.4's printed constant is not used. Inserting the printed M = (1/4)(3/2)^{1/3} into (1.9) gives about 0.213 rather than the printed (1/2)(3/4)^{1/4}, about 0.465, consistent with a disputed constant. The candidate explicitly avoids exchanging t -> infinity with alpha0 -> 0 and labels the static values as coefficients, not asymptotic constants. By homogeneity, total order 2k scales as t^{k beta}. Any truncation is therefore a nonnegative polynomial in t^beta, whose log divided by t^kappa tends to 0. The remark correctly says finite orders cannot fix the all-order factorial power.

minor: P:white-four statement: 'given by the following table or by exchanging the two chains' does not say that exchange relabels pairings. For (3,1) the map is A<->C, B->B, so J_{3,1,A} = J_{1,3,C}, not J_{1,3,A}; statically 1/640 versus 1/576. (E:total-four) uses only split sums and is correct. A one-line clarification would prevent misreading of individual entries.

The approximate-identity paragraph in the proof of P:white-four is terse. It does not state the continuity of the reduced area Psi(u,w) at (0,0) explicitly. It also does not say that the source's temporal truncation gamma^0_delta <= |.|^{-alpha0} converges monotonically. Both steps are elementary and implied, but one sentence each would make the passage self-contained.

Lemma L:static-four takes the static order-two value from G0 Lemma L:white-test. That lemma still evaluates the delta pointwise ('G at zero is 1/2'), as the G0 review already noted. G1's new approximate-identity argument covers order two equally well, but the text applies it only to order four.
Remark R:riesz-static: 'any fixed exponent abar in (alpha0,1)' is awkward while alpha0 is the varying parameter. It should read: fixed abar in (0,1) and 0 < alpha0 <= abar, as in L:static-four.

For the Riesz kernel, G1 does not restate that the source's regularized limit defining J_{m,n,D} equals the classical Lebesgue integral used in (E:riesz-two)-(E:riesz-four). The step is elementary in d=1: Gaussian smoothing satisfies p_eps*|.|^{-alpha} <= C|.|^{-alpha}, the Green factors are bounded and compactly supported, and the time truncation is monotone. It is also implicit in the source's (4.3) and G0's P:mixed. A sentence would close it.
In the calibration table, 'alpha0=0' rows should be labeled as the alpha0 down-to-0 coefficient limits, since the model requires alpha0>0. R:G1-scope already says this.

Abstract: 'computes finite-order white-space and Riesz coefficients' slightly overstates the Riesz order-four case, which is given only as an explicit integral representation without a closed form. Section 4 says this correctly.

Diagnostics only: in root-static-mc-results.json the (3,1) A and B estimates lie about 2.3-2.4 standard errors above the exact (1,3) C and B values, which must equal them by chain exchange. Taken together with the (1,3) row, this is consistent with sampling noise, and no proof depends on it.
